item.title: About
item.description: Personal Information I am a PhD student in Geography at the University of British Columbia, in Vancouver, Canada. Previously I earned an MSc in physics at University of British Columbia and a BS in physics at West Virginia University. My hobbies include backpacking, mountain biking, and whitewater kayaking. I welcome any emails to discuss science. Research Interests In my research I study sediment transport processes on Earth’s surface using mechanistic physics.

item.title: Teaching Experience
item.description: To date my teaching work has mainly involved teaching assistantships and course content development. Course Development I have a good deal of experience incorporating emerging virtual technologies into university courses: Produced four laboratory assignments with solutions and introductory materials for a fourth year Fluvial Geomorphology course. Topics included Flood Frequency Analysis, Sediment Entrainment, Sediment Transport of Mixtures, and Hydraulic Geometry. Produced a 45min Fluvial Geomorphology ``Virtual Field Trip" video documentary in collaboration with Bret Petersen and Marwan Hassan involving a tour of East Creek in the UBC Research Forest and pedagogical explanations of elements of reach-scale channel morphology, including step-pool sequences, the role of large wood, riffle-pool sequences, and bar dynamics.
